summary: Tested the Shared Internet Leads Queue end-to-end. Backend: 12 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_lead_queue_294.py covering queue summary, full queue, reps, claim/release/reassign, workflow queue timers + validation, and BOLA/ownership. 10/12 passed; both failures are a CRITICAL auth gap: every /api/leads/queue/* endpoint is completely unauthenticated (no token needed) and not covered by enforce_user_ownership. Frontend (Expo web, forest@imosapp.com): Home leads-waiting strip, Inbox 3-way toggle + badge, filter chips/counts, claim -> thread nav + toast, '...' menu release, manager reassign sheet + reassign back, and Admin > Lead Sources > Lead Queue Timers steppers/digest chips with save+reload persistence ALL work. One real defect found: a hard load / deep link of /inbox (or /inbox?segment=leads) renders the PUBLIC MARKETING page instead of the app inbox, which is exactly the URL used by the release-to-queue push notification. All app state and Website workflow timers restored to 5/15/10/30/18 and Alpha/Bravo/Charlie unclaimed, Delta/Echo claimed by forest (verified via API at the end).

critical.issue: No authentication at all. `curl` with NO Authorization header returns 200 with full lead data: GET /api/leads/queue/{FOREST_ID}/summary and /reps (leaks the entire 87-user roster with names/roles/open lead counts). Mutating routes are also open - POST /api/leads/queue/{uid}/release/{conv} without a token reaches the handler (returns 404 'Lead not found' for a fake id, i.e. it executes business logic), so an anonymous caller can release/reassign any lead. Root cause: server.py enforce_user_ownership ALWAYS_SKIP contains '/api/leads/' and is evaluated BEFORE PROTECTED_PREFIXES, so the '/api/leads/queue/' entry in PROTECTED_PREFIXES is dead code; routers/lead_queue.py itself has no Depends(auth)/request.state.user check. Expected 403 for cross-user and 401 without token.
Plain user (mjeast1985@gmail.com) token can read super-admin forest's queue summary (200 instead of 403) - BOLA. Same root cause as above.

This is the exact URL used in the lead_queue release push notification (send_push_to_user(..., '/inbox?segment=leads')) and in the Home strip fallback, so a rep tapping the 'Up for grabs' push lands on the marketing page. In-app navigation (Home strip tap -> /inbox?segment=leads&t=...) works fine.

rca_of_the_issue: enforce_user_ownership in /app/backend/server.py returns early for any path starting with a prefix in ALWAYS_SKIP, and that tuple includes '/api/leads/'. Because the ALWAYS_SKIP loop runs before the PROTECTED_PREFIXES match, the '/api/leads/queue/' entry added for this feature never executes, and routers/lead_queue.py has no auth dependency of its own - so all queue read and write endpoints are anonymous. Reproduce: `curl -s https://<base>/api/leads/queue/69a0b7095fddcede09591667/reps` (200 + full user roster) and `curl -X POST https://<base>/api/leads/queue/69a0b7095fddcede09591667/release/000000000000000000000000` (404 'Lead not found' - handler executed). Mitigation: narrow the ALWAYS_SKIP entry to the public lead intake path and add an explicit auth/self-or-manager guard in lead_queue.py.
